newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Eucalypt woodchips seen in new export battleground.
newsitem.headline: Eucalypt woodchips seen in new export battleground.

text.p: The world eucalypt woodchip export market is shaping up as a new battleground as plantations increasingly come on stream in South America and Indonesia to challenge Australian native forest sales to North Asian markets.

A report prepared for Western Australia's monopoly exporter of woodchip grade logs, Bunnings Forest Products, said it would be increasingly difficult to market Australian native pulpwood chips to Japan, the major market, because of new eucalypt plantations coming into production.
Bunnings, a division of Wesfarmers Ltd, presently exports 900,000 tonnes of woodchips a year, the report by consultants ACIL Economics and Policy Pty Ltd said.
The woodchip industry is worth about A$70 million a year in exports for Western Australia.

Japanese pulp and paper manufacturers are unlikely to continue sourcing woodchips from Western Australia native forests because of better quality, cheaper eucalypts now coming on the market in other countries, the report said.
South America is the main new supplier of plantation eucalypt. Chile is already a leading supplier of woodchips, with exports in 1995 amounting to more than four million tonnes.
Brazil also has been exporting since 1991, while Uruguay and Argentina are also emerging as significant exporters.

A Bunnings official told Reuters that while competition was intensifying, the company itself would have access to more than one million tonnes a year of plantation hardwood chips from year 2002/03 and would remain a big player in the export of plantation-grown eucalypt woodchips.

With current contracts for export to Japan to run to year 2005 for native woodchip, it was expected that native and plantation woodchip exports would continue together "in perpetuity", the spokesman said.
The company is confident it will be able to sell native woodchip despite inmcreasing competition from plantation eucalypts, the spokesman added.
Bunnings' main customers are the Japanese groups Hokuetsu Paper Mills Ltd, Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd and Nagoya Pulp Co Co.
